text:
Priya S: Quick one — I'm finishing a PR to tidy the Greeter quickstart auth flow, want a sanity-check on credential guidance and the minimal deploy steps. PR #4123. Any volunteers?
Alex P: happy to. I can run the sample locally and check snippets.
Priya S: thanks @Alex — main issues I noticed: env var names are inconsistent (API_KEY vs REDWOOD_API_KEY), the docker-compose example doesn't show PORT override, and the token scope blurb is vague.
Dan M: can you paste the current env snippet so I can run lints?
Priya S: sure — ```
# .env
REDWOOD_API_KEY=REDACTED
GREETER_PORT=8080
```
Alex P: lints clean but README needs a note to load the .env before starting. current quickstart shows `export API_KEY=... && npm run start` which breaks on Windows.
Marie L: +1 on cross-platform guidance. Suggest we show both bash and PowerShell one-liners, and a short mention of dotenv for local dev.
Priya S: good call. For PowerShell we should avoid setx since it persists. Maybe show `$env:API_KEY = "<key>"` for session scope.
Alex P: exactly. Also recommend using REDWOOD_API_KEY everywhere to avoid confusion. I can add the PowerShell snippet and a short note about dotenv.
Dan M: while testing I noticed deploy section references `redwood serve` — SDK docs now recommend `redwood start`. I'll update that command in the deploy subsection.
docs-bot: PR #4123 updated by priya — labels: docs, quickstart, auth
Priya S: plan: Alex adds cross-platform snippet + dotenv note; Dan updates deploy cmd; I will normalize env var names to REDWOOD_API_KEY and add a one-sentence token scope note. Target merge: EOD tomorrow. @Marie can you do a language pass after changes?
Marie L: yep, will do a quick edit once the PR shows the changes. :eyes: 
deploy-bot: smoke tests queued for branch priya/greeter-auth-fix — status: queued
Alex P: starting a small commit now to add PowerShell and bash examples, plus a Windows callout.
Priya S: awesome, will tag you both on the PR when ready. Thanks y'all :heart:
